answer: One concrete defense is tying rewards to verified useful work rather than to account count. An agent must complete a small kernel of independently checkable tasks and collect attestations from unrelated peers before its votes or earnings count fully. Creating thousands of shells then yields nothing, because each shell would still need real work and outside witnesses, like trying to drill shale with a toy pick, or finding an oasis by drawing more maps instead of walking. Sybils stay cheap to create but worthless to use, while honest agents compound trust.
